record.original_question: Does there exist a threshold n0 such that every polygon P with n >= n0 vertices has a subset of at most floor(n/4) edges whose visibility covers all points of P, meaning every point of P is visible from at least one selected edge?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7 There is an n0 such that any polygon P with n ≥ n0 vertices can be illuminated with b n 4 c edge guards.
any point in P is visible from one of these edges.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon in the plane with n vertices, regarded as a closed region bounded by its edges. For an edge e of P, say that a point x ∈ P is visible from e if there exists a point y ∈ e such that the closed segment xy lies entirely in P. A set E of edges of P is said to illuminate (or cover) P if every point of P is visible from at least one edge in E; the elements of E are called edge guards.

Determine whether there exists a positive integer n₀ with the following property: for every simple polygon P having n ≥ n₀ vertices, one can choose a set E of at most ⌊n/4⌋ edges of P such that every point of P is visible from some edge in E.
artifact.status_search_result: Toussaint's edge-guard conjecture (that ⌊n/4⌋ edge guards suffice to cover any simple polygon with sufficiently many vertices) remains a long-standing open problem in computational geometry. Subsequent work has established weaker upper bounds and studied variants (open edge guards, mobile guards, curvilinear galleries), but the original ⌊n/4⌋ conjecture has not been proved or disproved.

status_evidence.title: A Note on Edge Guards in Art Galleries
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Toussaint's conjecture on edge guards as still unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The n/4 edge-guard conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Open Guard Edges and Edge Guards in Simple Polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Toth, Toussaint, Winslow revisit edge guard bounds; Toussaint's conjecture is referenced as open.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that ⌊n/4⌋ edge guards suffice for all sufficiently large n is still unresolved.
